scenes.content: The AFDS is an integrated system that provides guidance and control through the Autopilot (AP) and Flight Director (FD) to maintain speed, altitude, and heading.

Mode Control Panel (MCP): The primary pilot interface;Flight Control Computers (FCC): The 'brains' processing the logic;Flight Management Computer (FMC): Provides long-term trajectory data;Autothrottle (A/T): Manages engine thrust settings
u(t) = K_p e(t) + K_i \int_{0}^{t} e(\tau) d\tau + K_d \frac{de(t)}{dt}
The system operates in two main axes: Lateral (LNAV/HDG) and Vertical (VNAV/FLCH). It calculates the error between the desired state and the current sensor data to drive the control surfaces.

LNAV: GPS-based horizontal path tracking;VNAV: Profile-based altitude and speed management;CMD (Command): Autopilot actively controls the servos;CWS (Control Wheel Steering): Pilot-assisted stabilization
